summary: OpenTripPlanner is a multimodal journey planning platform that combines OpenStreetMap geographical data with standard GTFS transit feeds. It computes routes across local public transport networks to provide travel itineraries.
goodFor: It suits transport authorities, researchers, or developers who need to run a self-hosted journey planner using standard open geographic and transit data.
watchOut: Ingesting and indexing large regional transit datasets and street networks can require substantial memory and processing resources.
deployNotes: Because the application runs on Java, you will typically need to configure appropriate heap size limits and place it behind a reverse proxy to handle TLS termination.
